evidence_adequacy.verdict: THIN: 5 transitions constrain rank 3 of 679 features, so the null space has dimension 676 and nearly every vector in it is a 'law' that is true over these states and unfalsified rather than confirmed. Treat every law below as a correlation awaiting a transition that could break it, not as a conservation law.

log.as: the dynamic set: icon1 rows30-35 cols11-16, icon2 rows36-41 cols11-16, tape1 rows32-33 cols17-22, tape2 rows38-39 cols17-22, meter (53,63)
log.subject: zero_space global_laws cell list
log.why: the enumerated cells sum to 36+36+12+12+1 = 97 = dynamic_cells and their bounding box is the reported box padded by one, so the decomposition is read off the engine's own output rather than inferred

log.as: Ink0..Ink6, seven types with arc-instances: all
log.subject: frame-0 colour partition of the 97 cells
log.why: counts 12/9/10/8/12/24/22 sum to 97, and 97 minus the 24 background-coloured ones equals cells_needing_an_owner = 73 exactly, so every dynamic cell gets exactly one owner

log.subject: mdl_segmenter obj0 / obj2 / obj3 (13x36, ~440 cells)
log.why: one canvas blob re-identified as a new track whenever any embedded pixel changes; connected_components(4) merges widget with canvas, and both variants report negative gain (-4037, -10409) by the engine's own measure

log.subject: mdl_segmenter obj1 (2x54, 108 cells, all 6 frames)
log.why: rows 53-54 of the window are constant across all six frames apart from the single corner pixel, which Ink2 already owns; a type here would claim 107 board cells twice

log.subject: the 4x4 colour-14 block at rows 31-34 cols 42-45
log.why: never appears in any diff and lies outside zero_space's dynamic cell list, so it is constant and the board explains it

log.subject: a3_hides_tape2_ones / a3_hides_tape2_twos
log.why: t3 changed exactly the 12 tape2 cells from their stripe colours to 4; the guard colored(above(above(?p)),4) is satisfied by all 12 and by none of the other 7 Ink1/Ink2 instances, checked cell by cell

log.subject: a7_hides_tape2_ones / a7_hides_tape2_twos
log.why: t5 is pixel-identical in effect to t3; duplicated only because the grammar has no `or` to join act=key(3) with act=key(7)

log.subject: a4_shows_tape2_ones / a4_shows_tape2_twos
log.why: t4 restored all 12 cells, each to its own frame-0 colour, which is why the two types need two rules; 8 to colour 1 and 4 to colour 2 matches the diff exactly

log.subject: a4_advances_the_corner_pixel
log.why: 1/1 on t4, and rightof(?p) = wall singles out (53,63) among all ten Ink2 instances; attribution to key(4) is the only one the guard language can state and the manual names the two rival readings

log.subject: any rule for key(1) or key(2)
log.why: the diff gave a count, a bounding box and two colour sets and no cell-level mapping; writing a rule would be inventing 96 pixels, so the manual predicts identity and declares the resulting 96-cell miss on t1 and t2 in advance

log.subject: adding colored(below(below(?p)),4) to the six tape rules
log.why: true of all 12 tape cells and excludes zero instance the existing atom had not already excluded, so it has no discriminating witness and fails the gain test; the confound is recorded and its probe named

log.subject: cegis_miner tracks obj0-obj3
log.why: all four refused, and the engine's own verdict that the world does not narrate as one mover is correct here -- nothing moved in six frames, everything recoloured in place

log.subject: constant 3999 + dynamic 97 = 4096 and 97 - 24 = 73
log.why: both identities close to the pixel against the store, which is what licenses seven colour-keyed types as a complete ownership scheme

log.subject: command-index parity as the meter law, carried from the previous level
log.why: parity predicts burns at indices 2 and 4; only index 4 changed the meter, so parity is refuted in this world and is not carried over

log.subject: s0 = s2, i.e. key(2) undoes key(1) on this state
log.why: distinct_states = 5 over 6 states forces exactly one coincidence, and s3, s4, s5 are pairwise separated by the tape and the meter, so the pair can only be s0 and s2

log.subject: the tape2 stripe pattern is colour 2 iff (row + col) mod 3 = 1
log.why: verified on all fourteen cells of rows 38-39 cols 16-22; recorded as description only, since no rule needs it and the two types already carry the restore colours

log.subject: press the key whose 96-cell diff was never itemised
log.why: the current frame is displayed in full, so making the other configuration current is the only way to obtain the pixel map that two missing rules need; cost is a declared 96-cell divergence

log.subject: press a hide-key while tape2 is already hidden
log.why: separates hide from toggle and converts an unwitnessed silence into a witnessed one; the manual currently asserts zero cells with no evidence at all

log.subject: press key(4) while the meter renders 3
log.why: the manual predicts twelve cells and no meter change; thirteen would refute colored(?p, 2) in a4_advances_the_corner_pixel and show the meter is a counter

log.subject: key(5) and key(6), never pressed
log.why: entirely unconstrained after six states; one of them is plausibly the pointer this menu-shaped board wants, and any pixel either moves is a whole action learned

log.subject: act=key(3) or act=key(7)
log.why: wanted one rule for two keys with identical observed effects; guards join with `and` only, so I wrote four rules where two would do and declared the duplication as an expressiveness cost, not a claim that the keys differ

log.subject: a click action carrying coordinates
log.why: wanted a rule for a pointer press on a specific cell; the guard language has nowhere to put two coordinates, so such a rule would fire on every click anywhere; wrote theorem two_keys_have_never_been_pressed_and_one_of_them_is_probably_a_pointer instead

log.subject: an explicit `unknown` successor for a (state, action) pair
log.why: wanted key(1) and key(2) to say `I decline to predict`; the compiled step is total, so absence of a rule emits identity in the same voice as knowledge, and the only remedy available was to state the 96-cell bill in prose before certify reports it

log.subject: an empty goal: section and a landmark without coordinates
log.why: the two constructs I can argue caused theory.py to fail to load; both are omitted entirely from this manual, and since I cannot run the compiler I say plainly that I do not know which one it was

log.subject: mdl_segmenter obj0/obj2/obj3 (~440-cell 13x36 blobs)
log.why: all three are the same connected component -- the colour-4 canvas with the widgets embedded in it -- re-identified as a new track whenever any interior pixel changes; the engine's own gain is negative (-4037 bits, -10409 bits), so by its own measure the segmentation loses to writing the pixels out.

log.as: board rows 53-54 plus the single Ink2 instance at (53,63)
log.subject: mdl_segmenter obj1 (2x54 bottom bar)
log.why: the bar is constant in every frame except its rightmost pixel, so 107 of its 108 cells are board by definition and the one that varies is already owned by Ink2.

log.as: the seven Ink types, one instance per dynamic cell, typed by frame-0 colour
log.subject: zero_space's enumerated 97-cell support
log.why: the enumeration is exactly icon1 36 + icon2 36 + tape1 12 + tape2 12 + meter 1 = 97 = dynamic_cells, and the per-colour census 12+9+10+8+12+24+22 closes to 97 with 97-24=73=cells_needing_an_owner and 4096-97=3999=constant_cells.

log.subject: the 24 cells of cols 17-22 at rows 30,31,34,35 that zero_space omits
log.why: they are the swap partners that hold canvas-4 on both sides, which is why a swap leaves them constant -- and their omission is what makes the changed count 96 rather than 144.

log.as: eighteen a1_* rules, one per (Ink type, destination colour)
log.subject: key(1) as a six-row block swap of rows 30-41 x cols 11-22
log.why: certify printed 24 divergent cells at t=0 and all 24 equal the current frame's colour six rows below them; independently, 72 partner pairs minus 24 canvas-on-both-sides pairs times 2 equals the reported 96 changed cells.

log.as: eight a2_* rules, one per Ink type
log.subject: key(2) as the inverse swap
log.why: s2 = s0 (distinct_states 5 against 6 states, and s3,s4,s5 are separated by the strip and the meter), so A2 from s1 restores every instance to its frame-0 colour, which is the same partner-copy specialised to that state.

log.as: guard free(below^6(?p)) on the lower-block Ink2 rules
log.subject: the Ink2 top/bottom split by free(six-below)
log.why: a lower Ink2's six-below lands in rows 44-45, background in every state; an upper Ink2's six-below lands in the lower block, which renders background only where icon1's field sits and that field is Ink5, never Ink2.

log.as: guard not rightof(?p) = wall on all five Ink2 swap rules
log.subject: excluding the meter from the swap rules
log.why: the meter has (47,63)=5 so a1_lower_ink2_takes_5 would fire on it whenever (59,63) renders background, and (59,63) is a cell no frame has ever shown; the diffs show the meter unchanged at t1 and t2.

log.subject: generalised hide/show rules for the strip after a swap
log.why: in s1 the stripe content is Ink4 and Ink5 instances at rows 32-33, and no transition has ever shown key(3), key(4) or key(7) acting on them; constraint 2 forbids the rule and the theorem the_hide_and_show_rules_are_pinned_to_rows_38_39 names the two-press probe that would witness it.

log.as: four rules where two would do
log.subject: a3/a7 hide rules written twice because the grammar has no `or`
log.why: key(3) and key(7) have identical 12-cell effects with one witness apiece and nothing separating them but frame count, and guards join with `and` only.

log.as: no move/jump/teleport event anywhere in the manual
log.subject: cegis_miner's verdict that the world does not narrate as one mover
log.why: the swap relocates 96 cells at once and every other transition is a recolour in place; nothing in six frames translates a single object.

log.subject: zero_space's single global law
log.why: its own evidence_adequacy says THIN -- 5 transitions constrain rank 3 of 679 features, null space dimension 676 -- so the law is unfalsified rather than confirmed; I kept its enumerated cell list, which is an observation, and left the law.

log.subject: a goal section
log.why: every state reports NOT_FINISHED, count(Ink2, color = 3) = 1 is already true in a plainly non-winning state, and arc-instances: all leaves no single instance to name; is_goal compiles to False and the playbook ranks by information instead.

log.subject: swap versus scroll-by-one
log.why: with two entries and wrapping the two permutations coincide; two presses of key(1) separate them, and a third configuration would mean my key(1) colour enumeration is complete only for the witnessed pair.

log.subject: hide versus toggle for key(3) and key(7)
log.why: the strip is hidden now, so my manual predicts silence with no witness; one press gives either a negative witness I lack or twelve cells that force four converse rules.

log.subject: the meter as one-shot versus counter
log.why: the meter renders 3 so a4_advances_the_corner_pixel cannot fire; key(4) from here predicts exactly twelve cells and no meter change, and thirteen refutes the colored(?p, 2) guard.

log.subject: whether key(3)/key(4)/key(7) address a screen row or a list entry
log.why: key(1) then key(4): twelve cells at rows 38-39 means row-addressed and my typed rules are accidentally right; twelve at rows 32-33 means entry-addressed and they are wrong in the swapped state.

log.subject: key(5) and key(6), never pressed
log.why: every other key is now ruled, so these two and a possible click are the only places a win condition or a new mechanism can still be hiding.

log.subject: copying a colour from one cell to another
log.why: I wanted one rule saying `?p takes the colour of the cell six rows away`; recolored takes an integer literal and colored takes an integer literal, so I wrote 26 rules enumerating every (type, destination colour) pair the witness exhibits, and the enumeration is complete for the witnessed configuration pair and for no other.

log.subject: a positional guard for `is this instance in the upper block`
log.why: there is no row predicate; I used the object types, which are frozen at frame 0 and therefore permanent, and split the one type spanning both blocks by free(below^6(?p)) plus a wall test for the meter.

log.subject: disjunction for key(3) and key(7)
log.why: guards join with `and` only, so act=key(3) or act=key(7) cannot be written and four rules do the work of two; if one grammar extension were available this is the one that would shorten the manual today.

log.subject: a third outcome meaning `unobserved, the manual declines to predict`
log.why: the compiled step is total, so my complete ignorance of key(5) is emitted in the same voice as my three-times-witnessed knowledge of key(3); only the theorem silence_is_a_prediction distinguishes them.
